title: Four gates to green
intro: TaskFlow already runs on your laptop. Turning that into a pipeline means four gates, each of which can only be entered from the one before — and the gate that stops you is the coverage gate, exactly as designed.

provenance.source: a narrated session against the shipped sample-project/taskflow; file paths, commands and the failure transcript are taken from the module, terminal output is reconstructed

foot: Run it for real: cd sample-project/taskflow && docker build -t taskflow:lab .

steps.title: Gate 1 — source to a hardened image
narrative: The shipped Dockerfile is the honest first draft: FROM python:3.12-slim, pip install, COPY . ., done. It builds and it runs, and it also ships the pip cache, the build toolchain, your .env if you forgot a .dockerignore, and a process running as root.

Hand Gemini the Dockerfile and requirements.txt together and ask for a multi-stage build with a non-root user and a health check. It has the dependency list in front of it, so it knows which wheels need a compiler at build time and which do not need one at runtime.
steps.youDo: gemini "@Dockerfile @requirements.txt Improve with multi-stage build, non-root user, health check. Output only the Dockerfile content."

terminal.text: gemini "@Dockerfile @requirements.txt Improve with multi-stage build, non-root user, health check. Output only the Dockerfile content."

Builder stage installs into /install with --prefix; runtime stage copies
only /install. cryptography and bcrypt need build tooling — that stays
in the builder and never reaches the final layer.

cells: pip cache and compilers ride along
a container escape starts with uid 0
81% smaller — pulls faster on every deploy
no root in the runtime layer
orchestrators can tell healthy from merely alive
none — left in the builder stage
smaller surface, nothing to compile with

steps.title: Gate 2 — one container becomes a service
narrative: docker run with three flags is fine until you need the same three flags tomorrow. docker-compose.yml makes the flags a file, and the interesting part is the volume: TaskFlow's database is sqlite:///./taskflow.db relative to WORKDIR /app, so the mount point has to be /app/taskflow.db or your data dies with the container.

Gemini gets that path by reading database.py and the Dockerfile together, not by guessing from the project name. Give it both, and give it main.py so it can wire the health check to the endpoint that actually exists.
steps.youDo: Generate the compose file, write a .env (never commit it), then docker compose up -d and check the health status.

terminal.text: gemini "@Dockerfile @database.py @main.py Generate docker-compose.yml with SQLite volume, .env file, restart policy, and health check."

steps.title: Gate 3 — CI stops you, and it is right to
narrative: The workflow Gemini generates ends with pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80, then a Docker build step that depends on it. Run it locally with act before you push, because a red run on GitHub costs a round trip and a red run on your laptop costs forty seconds.
It fails. Every test passes — and coverage is 72%, which is the number M08's coverage report already told you. auth.py at 58% and routers/tags.py at 56% are dragging the total under the line.
This is the gate working. The Docker build step never runs, because building an image from code whose auth paths are untested is exactly the thing the gate exists to prevent.

steps.title: Gate 4 — close the gap, then the pipeline runs end to end
narrative: Ask Gemini for tests against the specific uncovered lines, weighted the way you actually care: which of these gaps are security-critical? Without that steer it optimises for line count and writes you twelve tests for routers/tags.py. With it, it goes at auth.py lines 36-44 — malformed tokens, expired tokens, valid tokens for deleted users.
Twenty more tests, coverage at 95%, gate passes, Docker build runs, job succeeds. Toggle Before / After to watch the two blocked stages unblock.

Keep one thing in proportion: 95% line coverage means 95% of lines executed, not 95% of behaviour verified. A test that calls a function and asserts nothing raises coverage. The gate is a floor against neglect, not a proof of correctness.
steps.youDo: Generate the auth tests, re-run act, then docker compose down to clean up.

terminal.text: gemini "@auth.py @routers/tags.py Coverage: auth.py 58% missing 36-44,47,53-54; tags.py 56% missing 17,22-29,32-37. Which gaps matter most from a security perspective? Write pytest tests for the top 3."
